name: IgG4-Related Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: 2019 ACR/EULAR Classification Criteria for IgG4-Related Disease

criteria.description: Characteristic organ involvement (pancreas, biliary tree, salivary glands, lacrimal glands, retroperitoneum, aorta, kidneys, lungs)
Histopathology: dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with increased IgG4+ plasma cells (>10/HPF) and IgG4:IgG ratio >40%
Exclusion criteria: known malignancy, infection, or other autoimmune disease that better explains findings

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Entry criterion (characteristic clinical/radiologic involvement of typical organ) plus total inclusion/exclusion criteria score meeting classification threshold
diagnosticCriteria.notes: The 2019 ACR/EULAR criteria use a three-step process: (1) entry criteria (organ involvement), (2) exclusion criteria (must be absent), (3) inclusion criteria with weighted scoring across 8 domains. Serum IgG4 is elevated in only 50-70% of cases.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Tumefactive (mass-forming) lesions in multiple organs simultaneously
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic pattern of organ enlargement or mass formation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Storiform fibrosis with obliterative phlebitis on biopsy
pathognomonic.notes: Histologic hallmark; matted, swirling fibrosis pattern

common.notes: Formerly called Mikulicz disease; bilateral parotid, submandibular, or lacrimal gland enlargement

occasional.notes: Can mimic primary sclerosing cholangitis or cholangiocarcinoma

occasional.symptomName: Pulmonary nodules or interstitial lung disease

laboratory: Elevated serum IgG4 (>135 mg/dL; present in 50-70%)
Hypocomplementemia (low C3/C4; ~50%, especially with renal involvement)
imaging: CT/MRI: organ enlargement with delayed enhancement (pancreas, salivary glands, kidneys)
CT: sausage-shaped pancreas with capsule-like rim
MRCP: biliary strictures (can mimic PSC or cholangiocarcinoma)
CT: retroperitoneal soft tissue around aorta and ureters
PET-CT: FDG-avid lesions in multiple organs
other: Tissue biopsy (gold standard): dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, storiform fibrosis, obliterative phlebitis, IgG4+ plasma cells >10/HPF with IgG4:IgG ratio >40%
Core needle biopsy preferred over FNA (architectural assessment needed)

redFlags: Mass lesion mimicking malignancy (must exclude cancer, especially pancreatic/biliary)
Bilateral ureteral obstruction from retroperitoneal fibrosis
Compressive optic neuropathy from orbital disease
Failure to respond to glucocorticoids (reconsider diagnosis)
Progressive renal insufficiency from tubulointerstitial nephritis
references: Wallace ZS, et al. The 2019 American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism Classification Criteria for IgG4-Related Disease. Arthritis Rheumatol. 2020;72(1):7-19.
Deshpande V, et al. Consensus statement on the pathology of IgG4-related disease. Mod Pathol. 2012;25(9):1181-1192.
Stone JH, et al. IgG4-related disease. N Engl J Med. 2012;366(6):539-551.
